```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# Load and prepare Dataset 1 (PIEAEN01USM661N)
data1 <- read_csv("PIEAEN01USM661N.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    DATE = as.Date(DATE),  # Convert DATE column to Date format
    Value1 = as.numeric(PIEAEN01USM661N)  # Rename for clarity
  )

# Load and prepare Dataset 2 (A939RX0Q048SBEA)
data2 <- read_csv("A939RX0Q048SBEA.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    DATE = as.Date(DATE),  # Convert DATE column to Date format
    Value2 = as.numeric(A939RX0Q048SBEA)  # Rename for clarity
  )
```


```{r}
# Merge the two datasets by the DATE column
merged_data <- inner_join(data1, data2, by = "DATE")

# Scale Dataset 2 for dual-axis plotting
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(
    Value2_scaled = Value2 / max(Value2, na.rm = TRUE) * max(Value1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Create the plot using ggpubr
dual_axis_plot <- ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = DATE)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Value1, color = "Energy Price (Dataset 1)"), size = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Value2_scaled, color = "Real GDP (Dataset 2)"), size = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Energy Price (Original Scale)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * max(Value2, na.rm = TRUE) / max(Value1, na.rm = TRUE),
                        name = "Real GDP (Scaled)")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Energy Efficiency vs. Total Energy Consumption",
    x = "Year",
    color = "Dataset"
  ) +
  theme_pubr() +  # Use ggpubr's theme for a clean look
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Energy Price (Dataset 1)" = "blue", 
                                "Real GDP (Dataset 2)" = "red"))

# Print the plot
print(dual_axis_plot)


```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(ggpubr)

# Load Dataset 1 (PIEAEN01USM661N)
data1 <- read_csv("PIEAEN01USM661N.csv")

# Load Dataset 2 (A939RX0Q048SBEA)
data2 <- read_csv("A939RX0Q048SBEA.csv")

# Create the first line graph (Energy Price from Dataset 1)
plot1 <- ggplot(data1, aes(x = DATE, y = PIEAEN01USM661N)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Energy Price (Dataset 1)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Energy Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Create the second line graph (Real GDP from Dataset 2)
plot2 <- ggplot(data2, aes(x = DATE, y = A939RX0Q048SBEA)) +
  geom_line(color = "red", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Real GDP (Dataset 2)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Real GDP"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine both plots into one using ggarrange from ggpubr
ggarrange(plot1, plot2, 
          common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom",
          ncol = 1, nrow = 2)


```

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Load energy price data
energy_prices <- read_csv("EnergyPrices.csv")

# Load energy efficiency data
energy_efficiency <- read_csv("EnergyEfficiency.csv")

# Ensure DATE columns are properly formatted as Date objects
energy_prices$DATE <- as.Date(energy_prices$DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
energy_efficiency$DATE <- as.Date(energy_efficiency$DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Reshape data to long format for heatmap
energy_prices_long <- energy_prices %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -DATE, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Price")

energy_efficiency_long <- energy_efficiency %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -DATE, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Efficiency")


```

```{r}
# Merge the two datasets by DATE and Sector
heatmap_data <- inner_join(energy_prices_long, energy_efficiency_long, by = c("DATE", "Sector"))

# Create a heatmap
heatmap_plot <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = DATE, y = Sector, fill = Price)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue", name = "Energy Price") +
  labs(
    title = "Heatmap of Energy Prices by Sector",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Sector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Overlay a second heatmap for efficiency
efficiency_heatmap <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = DATE, y = Sector, fill = Efficiency)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "green", name = "Efficiency") +
  labs(
    title = "Heatmap of Energy Efficiency by Sector",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Sector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine the two heatmaps using patchwork
combined_heatmap <- heatmap_plot + efficiency_heatmap


```
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(gridExtra)

# Load energy price data
energy_prices <- read_csv("EnergyPrices.csv")

# Load energy efficiency data
energy_efficiency <- read_csv("EnergyEfficiency.csv")

# Ensure DATE columns are properly formatted as Date objects
energy_prices$DATE <- as.Date(energy_prices$DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
energy_efficiency$DATE <- as.Date(energy_efficiency$DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Reshape data to long format for heatmap
energy_prices_long <- energy_prices %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -DATE, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Price")

energy_efficiency_long <- energy_efficiency %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -DATE, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Efficiency")

# Merge the two datasets by DATE and Sector
heatmap_data <- inner_join(energy_prices_long, energy_efficiency_long, by = c("DATE", "Sector"))

# Create the first heatmap (Energy Prices)
heatmap_plot <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = DATE, y = Sector, fill = Price)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue", name = "Energy Price") +
  labs(
    title = "Heatmap of Energy Prices by Sector",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Sector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Create the second heatmap (Energy Efficiency)
efficiency_heatmap <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = DATE, y = Sector, fill = Efficiency)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "green", name = "Efficiency") +
  labs(
    title = "Heatmap of Energy Efficiency by Sector",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Sector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine the two heatmaps side by side
combined_heatmap <- heatmap_plot + efficiency_heatmap +
  plot_annotation(title = "Heatmap Comparing Energy Prices and Efficiency by Sector")

# Add policy discussion text
policy_text <- "Policy and Sustainability Implications:
- Policies that promote energy efficiency can reduce costs and carbon emissions.
- Monitoring sector-specific energy prices can help policymakers target subsidies or taxes effectively.
- Energy-intensive sectors (e.g., industrial and transportation) should prioritize efficiency improvements.
- Investment in renewable energy sources is crucial for long-term sustainability."

# Combine text and visualizations
dashboard <- grid.arrange(
  combined_heatmap,
  textGrob(policy_text, just = "left", gp = gpar(fontsize = 12)),
  ncol = 1,
  heights = c(2, 1)
)

# Save the dashboard as an image or display it
ggsave("Energy_Dashboard.png", plot = dashboard, width = 12, height = 8)


```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Load energy price data
energy_prices <- read_csv("EnergyPrices.csv")

# Load energy efficiency data
energy_efficiency <- read_csv("EnergyEfficiency.csv")

# Ensure DATE columns are properly formatted as Date objects
energy_prices$DATE <- as.Date(energy_prices$DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
energy_efficiency$DATE <- as.Date(energy_efficiency$DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Reshape data to long format for energy prices
energy_prices_long <- energy_prices %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -DATE, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Price")

# Reshape data to long format for energy efficiency
energy_efficiency_long <- energy_efficiency %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -DATE, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Efficiency")

# Merge the two datasets by DATE and Sector
heatmap_data <- inner_join(energy_prices_long, energy_efficiency_long, by = c("DATE", "Sector"))

# Create a combined heatmap
heatmap_plot <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = DATE, y = Sector, fill = Price)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue", name = "Energy Price") +
  labs(
    title = "Heatmap of Energy Prices by Sector",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Sector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Display the plot
print(heatmap_plot)


```
